subject.title: fix(openshell): bound sandbox readFile with size cap

question: Should OpenShell adopt the shared fs-safe bounded-read contract at its existing default, or should it define and support a distinct 100 MiB sandbox-read limit?
rationale: The correct API boundary is clear, but selecting a new user-visible resource limit changes which existing sandbox reads succeed and requires owner intent.

options.title: Adopt the shared fs-safe limit
options.body: Replace the custom loop with `root.read(..., { maxBytes })` using the repository’s established bounded-read contract and document the resulting OpenShell behavior.

options.title: Approve a distinct OpenShell cap
options.body: Keep a plugin-specific cap only after its value, compatibility impact, and shared fs-safe implementation path are explicitly agreed.

recommendation.title: Adopt the shared fs-safe limit
recommendation.body: Replace the custom loop with `root.read(..., { maxBytes })` using the repository’s established bounded-read contract and document the resulting OpenShell behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the existing security-sensitive pinned OpenShell file-read implementation.
